setup.zh: 立冬这天晌午，马三来收租。院子里摊着那头鹿，当门摆着一挂下水，娘坐在门槛里头等着。马三眯起眼睛：「黑松岭的鹿，姓什么？」
setup.en: Noon on the Start of Winter: Ma San comes for the rent. The deer lies spread over the yard, the offal right by the door, and your mother sits waiting inside the threshold. Ma San narrows his eyes: "The deer of Black Pine Ridge — what's their name?"

recap.zh: 皮抵了去年的欠，肉抵了今年的租，角也叫马三拿走了，他连爷爷的弓都摘了下来；娘问了一句「下水呢」，你编了一个吃饼、问「弓呢」的鬼，马三把弓扔了回来。娘理了理你的「围脖」，什么都没问。
recap.en: The hide went for last year's arrears, the meat for this year's rent, Ma San took the antlers too — and took Grandpa's bow down off the wall. Your mother asked, "And the offal?"; you made up a ghost that eats flatbread and asks "Where's the bow?", and Ma San threw the bow back. Your mother straightened your "scarf" and asked nothing.

zh: 皮，抵去年的欠；肉，抵今年的租。
en: The hide for last year's arrears; the meat for this year's rent.
"The bow that shot a Ma deer — its name is Ma too."

story.zh:
马三是晌午来的。马三把鹿皮往肩上一搭，道：「皮，抵去年欠下的；肉二十斤，抵今年的。」又拿短棍把那一地的肉拨了一遍，眼睛一眯：「一头鹿，四条腿。怎么只有三条？」

马小宝在他爹身后嚷道：「爹，阿禾说了，是头瘸腿的小母鹿！」马三看看那对比门框还宽的角，又看看儿子，一挥手：「母鹿长角？……称肉！」

秤称完了，马三却没有走。他慢悠悠地道：「黑松岭，是谁家的山？」马三道：「蒙山是马家的。黑松岭在不在蒙山上？」他爹道：「……在蒙山上。」马三道：「那黑松岭的鹿，姓什么？」

马三道：「山上的树姓马，山上的兔子姓马，山上的风都姓马。黑松岭上跑出来的鹿，倒姓了你家的姓？」「肉，我拿回去；角，我拿回去；皮，抵租。这叫公道。」「还有一样。射马家鹿的弓——也姓马。」他伸手便把那张弓从墙上摘了下来。

小满他爹扑通一声跪倒：「三爷！租交了！您说的，一张皮——」马三道：「皮是皮，弓是弓。」他掂了掂那张弓，「这叫连本带利。」

小满站在他爹身后，两只拳头不知什么时候已经攥紧了。他看了他娘一眼。他娘站了起来。她就站在门槛里头，说道：「三爷。下水呢？」

她道：「下水，也是马家的鹿身上的。三爷连弓都拿了，下水也拿去罢。」马三想了一会儿，大手一挥，道：「下水，赏你们了！」她道：「谢三爷。」

马三拎着那张弓，看出了神。然后他走回小满他爹跟前，压低了声音道：「黑松岭……你们进去了，还出来了？」他顿了一顿，「里头，还有什么？」
story.en:
Ma San came at noon. Ma San slung the hide over his shoulder. "The hide covers last year's debt. Twenty catties of meat covers this year's." Then he poked through the meat on the ground with his club, and his eyes narrowed: "One deer, four legs. Why are there only three?"

Behind his father, Ma Xiaobao piped up, "Pa, Ahe said it was a little doe with a lame leg!" Ma San looked at the antlers, wider than the doorframe, then at his son. He waved a hand. "A doe with antlers? …Weigh the meat!"

The weighing done, Ma San didn't leave. He said, taking his time: "Black Pine Ridge — whose mountain is that?" Ma San said, "Mount Meng belongs to the Mas. Is Black Pine Ridge on Mount Meng or isn't it?" His father said, "…It's on Mount Meng." Ma San said, "Then a deer from Black Pine Ridge — what's its name?"

Ma San said, "The trees on the mountain are named Ma, the rabbits on the mountain are named Ma, even the wind on the mountain is named Ma. And a deer that runs out of Black Pine Ridge goes by your family name?" "The meat, I take back. The antlers, I take back. The hide covers the rent. That's what's called fair." "And one more thing. A bow that shoots a Ma deer — is named Ma too." He reached out and took the bow down off the wall.

Xiaoman's father dropped to his knees with a thump. "Third Master! The rent's paid! You said it yourself, one hide—" Ma San said, "A hide is a hide. A bow is a bow." He weighed the bow in his hand. "This is what's called principal plus interest."

Xiaoman stood behind his father. At some point both his fists had clenched. He glanced at his mother. His mother stood up. She stood just inside the threshold and said, "Third Master. What about the offal?"

She said, "The offal came out of the Ma deer too. The Third Master's taken even the bow; take the offal as well." He thought for a while, then waved a big hand. "The offal — you can have it, as a gift!" She said, "Thank you, Third Master."

Ma San held the bow and somehow he got lost in looking. Then he went back to Xiaoman's father and said, lowering his voice, "Black Pine Ridge… you went in, and you came out?" He paused. "What else is in there?"

story_full.zh:
马三是晌午来的。

马小宝跟在后头，啃着一只酱鸭腿。

马三站在沈家院子里，看着那一地摊开的鹿，眼睛眯了起来。

他拎起那张鹿皮抖了几抖，问道：「黑松岭？」

小满他爹老老实实地道：「黑松岭。」

马三把鹿皮往肩上一搭，道：「皮，抵去年欠下的；肉二十斤，抵今年的。」

又拿短棍把那一地的肉拨了一遍，眼睛一眯：「一头鹿，四条腿。怎么只有三条？」

马小宝在他爹身后嚷道：「爹，阿禾说了，是头瘸腿的小母鹿！」门口有人「噗」地笑出了声，又赶紧咳嗽两声，把笑憋回了肚子里。马三看看那对比门框还宽的角，又看看儿子，脑门上的青筋一跳一跳，一挥手：「母鹿长角？……称肉！」

少的那一条腿，他懒得追；二十斤肉，总是够的。

家丁上来称肉，称满了二十斤，秤杆翘得跟马三的下巴一样高。

秤称完了，马三却没有走。他背着手，绕着那一地摊开的东西转了一圈，转到那对鹿角跟前，站住了，拿短棍敲了敲，

道：「这对角，不错。」

小满他爹道：「三爷喜欢，您拿去。」

马三道：「不是我喜欢。」他转过身来，看着他，慢悠悠地道：「黑松岭，是谁家的山？」

小满他爹一怔。

马三道：「蒙山是马家的。黑松岭在不在蒙山上？」

他爹道：「……在蒙山上。」

马三道：「那黑松岭的鹿，姓什么？」

院子里静了。半个村子的人都看着小满他爹。他的嘴唇动了两动，一个字也没说出来。他那双昨儿拉弓都不抖的手，这时候又抖了起来。

马三道：「山上的树姓马，山上的兔子姓马，山上的风都姓马。黑松岭上跑出来的鹿，倒姓了你家的姓？」他拿短棍往地上那堆肉一划，划了一个圈，「肉，我拿回去；角，我拿回去；皮，抵租。这叫公道。」说着眯起眼睛，往屋里瞧了一眼，瞧的是墙上那张缠着牛筋的旧弓，「还有一样。马家的鹿，是拿这张弓射的。射马家鹿的弓——也姓马。」

他一低头，侧着身子跨进门槛，伸手便把那张弓从墙上摘了下来。

小满他爹扑通一声跪倒：「三爷！租交了！您说的，一张皮——」马三道：「皮是皮，弓是弓。」他掂了掂那张弓，「这叫连本带利。」

小满站在他爹身后，两只拳头不知什么时候已经攥紧了。他比马三矮了两个头，马三手里还有那根包铁皮的短棍——打不过，就跑，娘说的。可这一回，他跑了，弓便没了。一张鹿皮，二十斤肉，崖上吊着的那根布绳，溪边那一箭，肩上那团凉下去的毛——统统抵了租，统统白搭，弓还是要姓马。他看了他娘一眼。他娘站了起来。

她没有走到马三跟前去，就站在门槛里头，说道：「三爷。下水呢？」

马三一愣，手里拎着弓，低头瞧了瞧当门那一挂鹿下水，皱起了眉头：「下水？」她道：「下水，也是马家的鹿身上的。三爷连弓都拿了，下水也拿去罢。」

马三瞧着那挂下水，又瞧了瞧她，脸上的横肉跳了两跳。这一挂下水，他要拿，往后石坳村的人提起马三，便要说一句「连人家的下水都拎走了」；他不拿，方才那番「马家的鹿」的话，便说得不大圆。他想了一会儿，大手一挥，道：「下水，赏你们了！」

她道：「谢三爷。」说完便坐下了，坐回门槛里头，两只手拢在袖子里。

马三拎着那张弓，低头看那弓背，看那一道一道缠着的牛筋，不知怎的，看出了神。然后他走回小满他爹跟前，压低了声音道：「黑松岭……你们进去了，还出来了？」他顿了一顿，「里头，还有什么？」
story_full.en:
Ma San came at noon.

Ma Xiaobao followed behind him, gnawing a soy-braised duck leg.

Ma San stood in the Shens' yard looking at the deer laid out all over the ground, and his eyes narrowed.

He picked up the deer hide, gave it a few shakes, and asked, "Black Pine Ridge?"

Xiaoman's father said, honestly, "Black Pine Ridge."

Ma San slung the hide over his shoulder. "The hide covers last year's debt. Twenty catties of meat covers this year's."

Then he poked through the meat on the ground with his club, and his eyes narrowed: "One deer, four legs. Why are there only three?"

Behind his father, Ma Xiaobao piped up, "Pa, Ahe said it was a little doe with a lame leg!" Someone at the gate snorted with laughter, then quickly coughed twice and swallowed the laugh back down. Ma San looked at the antlers, wider than the doorframe, then at his son, and the veins on his forehead throbbed. He waved a hand. "A doe with antlers? …Weigh the meat!"

The missing leg he couldn't be bothered to chase. Twenty catties of meat was there, anyway.

His men came forward and weighed the meat. They weighed out a full twenty catties, and the steelyard beam stuck up as high as Ma San's chin.

The weighing done, Ma San didn't leave. Hands behind his back, he took a turn round everything laid out on the ground, came to the antlers, and stopped. He tapped them with his club.

"Nice pair of antlers."

Xiaoman's father said, "If the Third Master likes them, take them."

Ma San said, "It isn't that I like them." He turned round, looked at him, and said, taking his time: "Black Pine Ridge — whose mountain is that?"

Xiaoman's father stopped short.

Ma San said, "Mount Meng belongs to the Mas. Is Black Pine Ridge on Mount Meng or isn't it?"

His father said, "…It's on Mount Meng."

Ma San said, "Then a deer from Black Pine Ridge — what's its name?"

The yard went quiet. Half the village was looking at Xiaoman's father. His lips moved twice, and not a word came out. Those hands that hadn't shaken drawing a bow yesterday began to shake again.

Ma San said, "The trees on the mountain are named Ma, the rabbits on the mountain are named Ma, even the wind on the mountain is named Ma. And a deer that runs out of Black Pine Ridge goes by your family name?" He drew his club across the heap of meat on the ground, drawing a circle round it. "The meat, I take back. The antlers, I take back. The hide covers the rent. That's what's called fair." Then he narrowed his eyes and looked into the house — at the old bow on the wall, the one wrapped in ox sinew. "And one more thing. The Ma deer was shot with that bow. A bow that shoots a Ma deer — is named Ma too."

He ducked his head, turned sideways, stepped over the threshold, reached out and took the bow down off the wall.

Xiaoman's father dropped to his knees with a thump. "Third Master! The rent's paid! You said it yourself, one hide—" Ma San said, "A hide is a hide. A bow is a bow." He weighed the bow in his hand. "This is what's called principal plus interest."

Xiaoman stood behind his father. At some point both his fists had clenched. He was two heads shorter than Ma San, and Ma San still had that iron-bound club in his hand — if you can't beat it, run, Ma had said. But this time, if he ran, the bow was gone. One deer hide, twenty catties of meat, the cloth rope hanging down the cliff, that arrow by the stream, the ball of fur on his shoulder going cold — all of it gone on the rent, all of it for nothing, and the bow would still be named Ma. He glanced at his mother. His mother stood up.

She didn't go over to Ma San. She stood just inside the threshold and said, "Third Master. What about the offal?"

Ma San stopped short, the bow hanging from his hand. He looked down at the string of deer offal in front of the door and frowned. "The offal?" She said, "The offal came out of the Ma deer too. The Third Master's taken even the bow; take the offal as well."

Ma San looked at the offal, then at her, and the knotted flesh of his face twitched twice. If he took the offal, then from now on whenever the people of Shi'ao Village mentioned Ma San they'd add, "He even carried off their offal." If he didn't, all that talk just now about "the Ma deer" wouldn't quite hold together. He thought for a while, then waved a big hand. "The offal — you can have it, as a gift!"

She said, "Thank you, Third Master." And with that she sat down, back inside the threshold, her hands tucked into her sleeves.

Ma San held the bow and looked down at its back, at the ox sinew wrapped on it turn after turn, and somehow he got lost in looking. Then he went back to Xiaoman's father and said, lowering his voice, "Black Pine Ridge… you went in, and you came out?" He paused. "What else is in there?"

label.zh: 踩爹的脚后跟，抢着装傻
label.en: Tread on Father's heel and play the fool

exits.means: plays dumb, says there is nothing in there, scared, hides what they saw

refuse.zh: 租还没交清——先把皮和肉过了秤。
refuse.en: The rent isn't settled — put the hide and the meat on the scale first.

story.zh:
他爹张嘴就要说。小满站在他爹身后，轻轻踩了一下他爹的脚后跟。小满抢着开了口——浑身上下抖得像一片秋风里的树叶——「三爷！里头……里头黑乎乎的，下大雨，我掉沟里了，差点就死了！还有鬼！」

马三眉头一皱：「什么鬼？」「有个白衣服的！没有脚，飘着走，头发老长老长，一直拖到地上——」「还吃饼！」马三一怔：「鬼吃饼？」

他的眼睛往马三手里一瞟，声音忽然压低了：「……吃完了饼，它还问我——」马三道：「问你什么？」小满道：「它问：『弓呢？』」

马三没有动。他脑门上冒出汗来，「吧嗒」，掉在那张弓的弓背上。「……你看清它的脸了？」小满道：「没脸。就一把白胡子。」

小满便接着抖：「它说，那张弓，是它的。谁拿了它的弓，它就跟谁回家。」他把弓往小满他爹怀里一扔，扔得又急又慌，倒像那弓烫手，骂了一声：「晦气！」

马小宝一把揪住了小满脖子上的「围脖」：「一股狗味儿。不过毛倒是软——拿回去，给我娘缝个领子。」小满两只手死死捂住了它：「小宝哥，这皮子……是黑松岭里捡的，就在那白胡子脚底下。」马小宝「嗷」的一声，那只手缩了回去。

马三回过头来，冲着满院子的人道：「都听着。打今儿起，谁敢靠近断碑一步，我打断他的腿。」马小宝瞧见阿禾蹲在篱笆里头，一脚踢翻了她搁在墙根的那只腌白菜坛子：「小母鹿？」

她把小满叫到跟前：「那个白衣服、没有脚、吃饼的鬼。」小满只得招认：「……娘，那是我编的。」「嗯。编得不好。」他娘顿了一顿，「鬼不吃饼。下回说它吃香火。」

他娘伸出手来，替他把脖子上那条「围脖」理了一理。她是看不见银月的——可她的手，偏偏停在了银月的背上。他娘说道：「小满，这条围脖，挺暖和的吧。」她什么都没问。

他爹朝黑松岭那边望了一眼，道：「断碑不让靠近了。这个冬天……」他娘道：「这个冬天，还长着呢。」
story.en:
His father opened his mouth to speak. Xiaoman, standing behind his father, trod lightly on his father's heel. Xiaoman got in first — and shook all over like a leaf in the autumn wind — "Third Master! In there… in there it's all black, and it was pouring, and I fell in a gully and nearly died! And there's a ghost!"

Ma San frowned. "What ghost?" "One in white! No feet, it floats along, its hair's ever so long, trailing right down to the ground —" "And it eats flatbread!" Ma San stopped. "A ghost that eats flatbread?"

His eyes flicked to Ma San's hand, and his voice suddenly dropped: "…And when it finished the flatbread, it asked me—" Ma San said, "Asked you what?" Xiaoman said, "It asked: 'Where's the bow?'"

Ma San didn't move. Sweat broke out on his forehead, and fell — *plip* — onto the back of the bow. "…Did you see its face clearly?" Xiaoman said, "No face. Just a white beard."

Xiaoman kept shaking: "It said that bow is its bow. Whoever takes its bow, it follows them home." He threw it into the arms of Xiaoman's father, threw it fast and flustered, as though the bow were burning his hand, and swore: "Bad luck!"

Ma Xiaobao grabbed the "scarf" round Xiaoman's neck. "Smells like dog. The fur's soft, though — I'll take it home and have Ma sew a collar out of it." Xiaoman clamped both hands over it: "Brother Xiaobao, this pelt… I picked it up in Black Pine Ridge, right under that white beard's feet." Ma Xiaobao gave a yelp. His hand shot back as if it had been singed.

Ma San turned round and said to everyone in the yard, "Listen, all of you. From today, anyone who goes one step near that broken stone, I'll break his legs." Ma Xiaobao saw Ahe crouching inside the fence and kicked over the crock of pickled cabbage she'd set by the foot of the wall: "Little doe, eh?"

She called Xiaoman over: "That ghost in white, with no feet, that eats flatbread." Xiaoman had to own up. "…Ma, I made it up." "Mm. You made it up badly." His mother paused. "Ghosts don't eat flatbread. Next time say it eats incense."

His mother reached out and straightened the "scarf" round his neck. She couldn't see Yinyue — and yet her hand came to rest right on Yinyue's back. His mother said, "Xiaoman, that scarf's nice and warm, isn't it." She didn't ask anything.

His father looked off towards Black Pine Ridge. "We're not allowed near the broken stone now. This winter…" His mother said, "This winter has a long way to go yet."

story_full.zh:
他爹张嘴就要说。他爹这个人，这辈子不会撒谎，人家问什么，他便答什么。他要是把那道摔不死人的山谷、谷里会发亮的草和会响的银叶子说出来，马三明天便会带着二十条猎狗、几十个家丁进去，把那道山谷翻个底朝天。

小满站在他爹身后，轻轻踩了一下他爹的脚后跟。

他爹一愣，嘴张着，没出声。小满抢着开了口——一面说，一面缩着脖子，两只手抱着胳膊，浑身上下抖得像一片秋风里的树叶——「三爷！里头……里头黑乎乎的，下大雨，我掉沟里了，差点就死了！还有鬼！」

马三眉头一皱：「什么鬼？」

「有个白衣服的！」小满抖得更厉害了，「没有脚，飘着走，头发老长老长，一直拖到地上——三爷，那地方真不能去，我爷爷就是在那儿没的！」

院子里好几个婆娘已经拿手捂住了嘴，眼睛瞪得一个比一个圆。

马三道：「……白衣服的？」

「还吃饼！」

马三一怔，两道眉毛一高一低，拧成了两个疙瘩：「鬼吃饼？」

「吃得可香了！」小满拿手比了一比，「我娘烙的饼，这么厚一张，它三口就吃完了，一面吃还一面嫌难吃！」

说到这里，他的眼睛往马三手里一瞟，声音忽然压低了，压得只剩一口气：「……吃完了饼，它还问我——」

马三道：「问你什么？」

小满道：「它问：『弓呢？』」

马三没有动。他脑门上冒出汗来，黄豆大的一颗，顺着鼻梁滚到鼻尖上，挂了一挂，「吧嗒」，掉在那张弓的弓背上。过了半晌，他的嗓子有点发干，道：「……你看清它的脸了？」

小满道：「没脸。就一把白胡子。」

马三的手，这才抖了一抖，喉咙里「咕咚」一声，咽下一大口唾沫。小满便接着抖，从头顶抖到脚跟，抖到后来，牙齿也咯咯地打起架来：「它说，那张弓，是它的。谁拿了它的弓，它就跟谁回家。」他心里却一面抖，一面暗道：银月，对不住。你要是醒着，准要咬我。抖着抖着，他自己也分不清了：这一身抖，有几分是装的。

马三的脸，先是红，跟着变紫，又跟着变黑，最后变成了那一种颜色。他瞧着手里那张弓，像瞧着一条盘起来的蛇。半晌，他把弓往小满他爹怀里一扔，扔得又急又慌，倒像那弓烫手，骂了一声：「晦气！」

马小宝却不怕。他跟在他爹身后，走过小满身边，忽然伸出那只油乎乎的手，一把揪住了小满脖子上的「围脖」，凑到鼻子底下闻了闻：「一股狗味儿。不过毛倒是软——拿回去，给我娘缝个领子。」小满两只手死死捂住了它，脸上却抖得更凶了：「小宝哥，这皮子……是黑松岭里捡的，就在那白胡子脚底下。」马小宝「嗷」的一声，那只手像给火燎了一下，缩了回去，一张胖脸白得像刚出笼的馒头，在衣裳上蹭了三遍，道：「……谁稀罕。一张狐狸皮，我家要多少有多少。」

马三已走到了门口，又回过头来，冲着满院子的人道：「都听着。打今儿起，谁敢靠近断碑一步，我打断他的腿。」说罢一跺脚，走了。

马小宝跟在后头，走过老周家门口，瞧见阿禾蹲在篱笆里头，一脚踢翻了她搁在墙根的那只腌白菜坛子：「小母鹿？」坛子在地上滚了两滚，那一个秋天的白菜叶子，撒了一地。

马家的人走远了，看热闹的人也散了。他爹把那张弓挂回墙上，挂了两回才挂稳，又蹲下去，把那挂下水捧了起来，捧得很小心。他道：「……这个，给老周家。赔白菜。」

他娘道：「嗯，我送过去。」

他爹又道：「棉袄……」

他娘道：「不急。」

说着把两只手往袖子里拢了拢。她那件棉袄，是嫁过来那年做的，袖子短了一截，一拢，手腕便露在外头，冻得发红。

她把小满叫到跟前，看了他很久，才道：「那个白衣服、没有脚、吃饼的鬼。」

小满只得招认：「……娘，那是我编的。」

「嗯。编得不好。」他娘顿了一顿，「鬼不吃饼。下回说它吃香火。」

小满一愣：「为什么？」

他娘道：「鬼吃饼，马三会想，那是个饿死鬼，饿死鬼好打发，扔两张饼就是了。鬼吃香火，那就是有人供着的，有人供着的鬼，马三惹不起。」

他娘伸出手来，替他把脖子上那条「围脖」理了一理。她是看不见银月的——可她的手，偏偏停在了银月的背上，停了一停。小满低头一看，只见围脖里那只昏迷的小狐狸，耳朵轻轻地动了一下。

他娘说道：「小满，这条围脖，挺暖和的吧。」

她什么都没问。他爹捧着那挂下水，站在门口，朝黑松岭那边望了一眼，道：「断碑不让靠近了。这个冬天……」他娘道：「这个冬天，还长着呢。」
story_full.en:
His father opened his mouth to speak. His father was a man who had never told a lie in his life; whatever people asked, he answered. If he told about that valley you couldn't die falling into, the grass in it that glowed and the silver leaves that rang, then tomorrow Ma San would take twenty hounds and dozens of men in there and turn that valley upside down.

Xiaoman, standing behind his father, trod lightly on his father's heel.

His father stopped, mouth open, without a sound. Xiaoman got in first — and as he spoke he hunched his neck down, clutched his arms, and shook all over like a leaf in the autumn wind — "Third Master! In there… in there it's all black, and it was pouring, and I fell in a gully and nearly died! And there's a ghost!"

Ma San frowned. "What ghost?"

"One in white!" Xiaoman shook harder. "No feet, it floats along, its hair's ever so long, trailing right down to the ground — Third Master, you really can't go there, that's where my grandpa died!"

Several of the women in the yard had already clapped their hands over their mouths, each pair of eyes rounder than the next.

Ma San said, "…In white?"

"And it eats flatbread!"

Ma San stopped. His two eyebrows went one up and one down and screwed themselves into two knots. "A ghost that eats flatbread?"

"Gobbles it up!" Xiaoman showed with his hands. "My ma's flatbread, this thick, and it finished it in three bites, and the whole time it was eating it kept saying it was disgusting!"

At this point his eyes flicked to Ma San's hand, and his voice suddenly dropped, dropped till it was only a breath: "…And when it finished the flatbread, it asked me—"

Ma San said, "Asked you what?"

Xiaoman said, "It asked: 'Where's the bow?'"

Ma San didn't move. Sweat broke out on his forehead, a drop as big as a soybean, which rolled down the bridge of his nose to the tip, hung there, and fell — *plip* — onto the back of the bow. After a long moment, his throat a little dry, he said, "…Did you see its face clearly?"

Xiaoman said, "No face. Just a white beard."

Only then did Ma San's hand give a shake, and his throat went *gulp* as he swallowed a big mouthful of spit. Xiaoman kept shaking, shook from the top of his head to his heels, shook until his teeth were chattering too: "It said that bow is its bow. Whoever takes its bow, it follows them home." But inside, even as he shook, he was thinking: Yinyue, sorry. If you were awake you'd bite me for sure. Shaking and shaking, he himself couldn't tell any more how much of all this shaking was put on.

Ma San's face went red first, then purple, then black, and in the end it turned that colour. He looked at the bow in his hand as if it were a coiled snake. After a long moment he threw it into the arms of Xiaoman's father, threw it fast and flustered, as though the bow were burning his hand, and swore: "Bad luck!"

Ma Xiaobao, though, wasn't afraid. Following his father, he walked past Xiaoman and suddenly reached out his greasy hand, grabbed the "scarf" round Xiaoman's neck, and brought it up under his nose to sniff. "Smells like dog. The fur's soft, though — I'll take it home and have Ma sew a collar out of it." Xiaoman clamped both hands over it, and his face shook harder than ever: "Brother Xiaobao, this pelt… I picked it up in Black Pine Ridge, right under that white beard's feet." Ma Xiaobao gave a yelp. His hand shot back as if it had been singed, his fat face went as white as a bun fresh out of the steamer, and he wiped it on his clothes three times. "…Who wants it? A fox pelt — we've got as many of those as we like at home."

Ma San had reached the gate. He turned round and said to everyone in the yard, "Listen, all of you. From today, anyone who goes one step near that broken stone, I'll break his legs." With that he stamped his foot and left.

Ma Xiaobao followed. Passing Old Zhou's gate, he saw Ahe crouching inside the fence and kicked over the crock of pickled cabbage she'd set by the foot of the wall: "Little doe, eh?" The crock rolled over twice on the ground, and a whole autumn's worth of cabbage leaves spilled out across it.

The Ma people had gone off, and the onlookers had gone too. His father hung the bow back on the wall — it took him two tries to get it to stay — then crouched and gathered up the string of offal, very carefully. He said, "…This goes to Old Zhou's family. To make up for the cabbage."

His mother said, "Mm. I'll take it over."

His father said, "The padded jacket…"

His mother said, "No hurry."

And she tucked her two hands into her sleeves. That padded jacket of hers had been made the year she married into the family; its sleeves were too short by a good bit, and when she tucked her hands in, her wrists stuck out, red with cold.

She called Xiaoman over and looked at him a long time before she said, "That ghost in white, with no feet, that eats flatbread."

Xiaoman had to own up. "…Ma, I made it up."

"Mm. You made it up badly." His mother paused. "Ghosts don't eat flatbread. Next time say it eats incense."

Xiaoman stopped. "Why?"

His mother said, "A ghost that eats flatbread — Ma San will think it's a starved ghost, and starved ghosts are easy to get rid of; throw them a couple of flatbreads and that's that. A ghost that eats incense is one that somebody's worshipping. A ghost with somebody worshipping it is one Ma San can't afford to cross."

His mother reached out and straightened the "scarf" round his neck. She couldn't see Yinyue — and yet her hand came to rest right on Yinyue's back, and rested there a moment. Xiaoman looked down and saw the little unconscious fox in the scarf twitch an ear, very slightly.

His mother said, "Xiaoman, that scarf's nice and warm, isn't it."

She didn't ask anything. His father, holding the string of offal, stood in the doorway and looked off towards Black Pine Ridge. "We're not allowed near the broken stone now. This winter…" His mother said, "This winter has a long way to go yet."

story.zh:
他爹张嘴就要说。他爹这个人，这辈子不会撒谎，人家问什么，他便答什么，这是他最大的本事，也是他最大的毛病。他要是把那道摔不死人的山谷、谷里会发亮的草和会响的银叶子说出来，马三明天便会带着二十条猎狗、几十个家丁进去，把那道山谷也篦一遍，篦得比他娘梳头还细。

小满在后头伸脚去踩他爹的脚后跟——踩空了。他爹已经一五一十地说了：「里头的树，比外头高一倍。鹿，比前山的大一圈。就是路不好走，下起雨来——」

马三的眼睛一下子亮了，亮得像两盏刚点上的油灯。他掂了掂手里那张弓，忽然把它往小满他爹怀里一塞，道：「大一圈？好。弓，你留着。黑松岭的鹿，今年起，也姓马了——马家的狗不进那块碑，你进。明年开春，你拿这张弓，进去给马家打。」说罢转身便走。

小满看着他爹怀里那张弓。弓是留下了，可从今往后，它射出去的每一支箭，都姓马。

马小宝跟在他爹身后，走过小满身边的时候，冲他挤了挤眼睛：「哟，沈小满，还活着呢？命挺硬啊。」小满低下头道：「托小宝哥的福。」马小宝很满意。小满不太满意。

马家的人一走，他娘便把小满拉进屋，关上了门，看着他，看了很久，才叹了口气，道：「你爹那张嘴。娘管了二十年，没管住。」

她伸出手来，替他把脖子上那条「围脖」理了一理。小满登时愣住了。她是看不见银月的，在她眼里，那不过是一条灰不溜秋的旧狗皮——可她的手，偏偏停在了银月的背上，停了一停。小满低头一看，只见围脖里那只昏迷的小狐狸，耳朵轻轻地动了一下。

他娘说道：「小满，这条围脖，挺暖和的吧。」

她什么都没问，转身去灶间了。
story.en:
His father opened his mouth to tell. He couldn't lie to save his life: whatever he was asked, he answered — his greatest skill and his greatest failing. If he told about that valley you could fall into and live, the grass in it that glowed and the silver leaves that rang, then tomorrow Ma San would take twenty hounds and dozens of servants in there and comb that valley through, finer than his mother combed her hair.

Xiaoman reached out a foot behind to tread on his father's heel — and missed. His father was already telling it, every detail: "The trees in there are twice as tall as outside. The deer, a size bigger than the front hills'. Only the going's bad, and when it rains —"

Ma San's eyes lit up at once, like two lamps just lit. He weighed the bow in his hand, then shoved it into Xiaoman's father's arms. "A size bigger? Good. Keep the bow. From this year, the deer of Black Pine Ridge are named Ma too — the Ma dogs won't pass that stele, but you will. Come spring, you take this bow in there and hunt for the Mas." And he turned to go.

Xiaoman looked at the bow in his father's arms. The bow had stayed — but from now on, every arrow it loosed would be named Ma.

Ma Xiaobao, following his father, winked at Xiaoman as he passed. "Well, Shen Xiaoman, still alive? Tough little life you've got." Xiaoman lowered his head. "All thanks to you, Xiaobao-ge." Ma Xiaobao was very satisfied. Xiaoman was not.

The moment the Mas were gone his mother pulled Xiaoman inside and shut the door, and looked at him a long time before she sighed. "Your father's mouth. Twenty years I've tried to govern it, and never managed."

She reached out and straightened the "scarf" round his neck. Xiaoman froze. She couldn't see Yinyue; to her it was a scruffy old grey dog pelt — yet her hand stopped right on Yinyue's back, and rested there a moment. Xiaoman looked down: the unconscious little fox inside the scarf had moved one ear, very slightly.

His mother said, "Xiaoman, that scarf's nice and warm, isn't it."

She asked nothing, and turned and went into the kitchen.
